Subject: Commercial model clarifications for RFI — burst/true‑up behavior

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the initial RFI pack — couple of commercial clarifications from our finance and platform teams before we proceed to the SOW stage:  

1) Burst handling: if we spike 6x our commit for a single day, how are overages billed and do you provide short‑term credits?  
2) Smoothing/true‑up: can you outline the true‑up cadence, lookback window, and whether unused committed tokens can be carried forward?  
3) Invoice treatment: are burst overages invoiced as postpaid usage each month or consolidated into a quarterly true‑up invoice?  
4) Discount flexibility: are there any conditional discount tiers for model mix shifts (e.g., 40% embeddings + 60% chat vs 90% chat)?

Appreciate a short written summary plus any appendix you can share. We have a procurement review on Friday and would like to lock the commercial approach.

Thanks,
Katherine Li
Sr. Procurement Manager — GlobeX

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Katherine Li <katherine.li@globexcorp.com>
Cc: derek.shaw@globexcorp.com
Date: 2027-06-14T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial model clarifications for RFI — burst/true‑up behavior

Katherine — thanks for the clear list. High level first, then I attached a short pricing appendix (RI_Pricing_Appendix_v3.pdf) and a sample mutual action plan (GX_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx). Key points below — happy to walk through on a 30m call.

1) Burst handling (day spikes):
- Short bursts (defined as any day where daily consumption > 300% of committed daily run‑rate) are billed as standard overage usage at the published overage rate for the model family used (see appendix page 2).
- We automatically apply a temporary burst credit cushion for the first 72 hours of a new spike (one‑time per spike event) to avoid immediate SLA/expense surprises for transient load. That cushion = up to 5% of monthly commit in token equivalents and is applied before invoiceable overage.
- Example: 1M monthly commit; one‑day 6x spike consumes additional 250k tokens above expected daily throughput. The first 50k tokens (5% cushion) are covered by the burst credit; remaining charged at overage rate.

2) Smoothing and true‑up cadence:
- Monthly usage is reported and invoiced in arrears. True‑up occurs quarterly by default (end of Q), reconciling committed vs actual usage across the quarter.
- Lookback window for smoothing decisions is 90 days; customers can opt into monthly true‑ups for tighter control.
- Carryforward policy: unconsumed committed tokens can be carried forward up to one subsequent quarter (prorated) when enrolled in our "Commit Carryforward" addendum. Unused credits beyond that expire.

3) Invoice treatment:
- Overage billing default: line‑itemed on monthly invoice (postpaid) to reflect real usage.
- Quarterly true‑up consolidates committed shortfalls or credits and issues a single reconciliation invoice or credit memo.
- For enterprise customers that prefer consolidated billing, we offer a quarterly consolidated invoice option (single invoice combining monthly usage + reconciliation).

4) Discount buckets & model mix shifts:
- Discounts are applied to committed spend by model family (low‑cost embedding family vs standard chat family vs high‑capacity LLM family). If your model mix shifts and spend reweights > 20% across families within a quarter, we provide a one‑time model‑mix adjustment to the tiering ladder for the following quarter (subject to review).
- Conditional uplift discounts (e.g., additional 5% off overage) are available if you enroll in a 12‑month committed volume plan for combined LLM + embeddings. Specifics are in appendix (section 4).

Operational notes:
- Auto‑burst fallback: if Dedicated capacity is full, we will route excess traffic to compatible hosted variants to avoid failure; that routing is billed at the compatible model's rate and counted in overage.
- Alerts: we can configure consumption alerts at % of commit, absolute tokens, and forecasted 7‑day burn.

Next steps: review the attached appendix (page 3 has a worked numeric example), choose quarterly vs monthly true‑up, and I'll send an updated MSA appendix for signatures. If useful, I can propose a call on Thursday afternoon.

Regards,
Logan Wright

Looping you both for pricing ops and approval on the proposed burst cushion + carryforward concession. Quick thoughts:
- Approve 5% one‑time cushion by default but cap to 50k tokens for pilot customers — otherwise we expose margin on extreme spikes.
- Approve carryforward for 1 quarter but only with annual commit or prepay option enabled (protects finance).
- If GlobeX wants monthly true‑ups, require a 6% admin fee to cover increased invoicing cadence.

Ben — can you confirm the overage ladder we referenced in the appendix aligns with current pricing playbook and note any margin impacts?

Marissa
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

Katherine — quick follow up after internal review. We've captured the GlobeX requests and proposed the following commercial approach for your procurement review:  

1) Default workflow: monthly postpaid usage + quarterly reconciliation true‑up.
2) Burst cushion: 5% of monthly commit, max 50k tokens per distinct spike event, applied automatically for first 72 hours.
3) Carryforward: up to 1 subsequent quarter, available if you sign annual commit or choose the prepay option in section A of the appendix.
4) Invoice options: monthly line items by default; consolidated quarterly invoice available on request.
5) Model mix: one model‑mix tier adjustment allowed per quarter for reweight >20%; significant persistent reweights subject to contract amendment.

Attachments: RI_Pricing_Appendix_v3.pdf (pricing ladder, worked examples), GX_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (SOW timeline + milestones).

If this aligns with GlobeX's procurement preferences I can:  
- Draft the pricing appendix into the MSA (redlines for carryforward and burst cap), and
- Send a DocuSign link for the MA P and pricing appendix or book a 30‑minute call to walk procurement through the worked example.
